independent.summary: A page failure mid-walk leaves the sidebar showing a silently truncated workspace: `sidebarLoading` is already false, the rejection has no catch anywhere (`onMounted(() => loadEntities())` in WikiLayout.vue:574, no global error/unhandledrejection handler in the client), so a 500 or network blip on page 3 of 5 renders a partial list that is indistinguishable from a complete one — before this change a failed load left the list empty, which at least looked wrong.

The sort became `{ title: 1, _id: 1 }` while `Entity`'s only index is `{ workspaceId: 1, title: 1 }`, so every list read — paged and unpaged — now needs a blocking in-memory sort of the whole matching set; the paged path therefore still fetches and sorts the entire workspace per page (only serialization is bounded), and the unpaged read that MCP/graph/search still use got strictly more expensive than before (acknowledged as a follow-up in the Decision Log, not fixed here).

`entities.value = [...collected]` on every page reverts any concurrent change to the list made while pages 2..N are in flight: `removeEntity`'s filter, `editEntity`'s in-place slot replacement and an SSE-driven refresh all act on `entities.value`, while `collected` still holds the pre-change objects, so a deleted row reappears or an edit un-paints until the next full load — a window that was one request before and is now the whole multi-page walk.

grades.reason: Accurate about this code: a failing page rejects into a caller that never catches, `sidebarLoading` is already cleared, and the user is left with a partial list and no error — the same defect as my independent finding 1 (the suggested rollback is not the fix, but the failure scenario is real).
The first test in that file asserts `getEntityPage.mock.calls` equals `[{limit:200, after:null},{limit:200, after:CURSOR}]`, which is exactly the claim the finding says is unverified.
`total` is never read by the composable (only the server tests assert it), so there is nothing for this test to verify and no defect in not verifying it.

Untrue in this code: the cursor carries `_id` and the clause is `{$or:[{title:{$gt:t}},{title:t,_id:{$gt:id}}]}` with sort `{title:1,_id:1}`, and the same-title fixture walk at limit 1 pins that each duplicate title is served exactly once.
No-limit-means-unpaged is the item's explicit, documented requirement (keeping the bare array so MCP/chat/outside callers are not broken), not a validation defect.
Restates finding 4 and is equally untrue: `nextAfter` is the last served row's `(title, _id)` and the `_id` tie-break makes the next page strictly after it.

The order is the opposite of what is claimed — every `process.env` assignment (including `delete process.env.BEARER_TOKEN`) runs before both dynamic imports, which is precisely why the import is dynamic.
`BOB_ENTITY` and `BULK_PREFIX` are module constants defined in the same file (lines 128 and the pagination block), not untrusted inputs a test could or should validate.
Same void claim as 8 for `BIG`, which is a literal defined at line 111 of the test file.

summary: One of nine findings lands (the silent partial-list failure), the other eight are either contradicted by the code they cite or are content-free complaints about test constants, and the triage is right except for calling auth touched on the strength of a line that is about cursor validation.
